q: Glycerol, which has three -OH groups, is classified as
why: Glycerol has three hydroxyl groups, making it a trihydric alcohol.

q: The IUPAC name of CH3-O-CH3 is
why: Ethers are named as alkoxyalkanes in IUPAC; CH3-O-CH3 is methoxymethane.

q: The industrial cumene process converts cumene into phenol and which useful by-product?
why: Cumene hydroperoxide, on acid hydrolysis, gives phenol and acetone as a valuable by-product.

q: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol mainly because
o: Phenol has a lower molecular mass
The phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance with the ring
why: Resonance delocalises the negative charge of phenoxide into the benzene ring, stabilising it, unlike the alkoxide ion.

q: A nitro (-NO2) substituent on the phenol ring, compared to unsubstituted phenol, will
why: Electron-withdrawing -NO2 further stabilises the phenoxide ion by resonance/induction, increasing acidity.

q: In Williamson's ether synthesis, R-O-Na reacts with R'-X mainly via
why: The alkoxide nucleophile attacks a primary alkyl halide in a single-step SN2 displacement.

q: In the Lucas test, which alcohol gives turbidity immediately at room temperature?
why: Tertiary alcohols form the most stable carbocation fastest via SN1, giving immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent.

q: A neutral FeCl3 solution added to phenol gives
why: Phenols form a coloured complex with neutral FeCl3, giving a characteristic violet/purple colour; alcohols do not react.

q: Dehydration of an alcohol with conc. H2SO4 at about 413 K with excess alcohol mainly gives
why: At the lower temperature of about 413 K (140 C), intermolecular dehydration dominates, forming an ether.

q: Ethanol + acetic acid with conc. H2SO4 catalyst undergoes Fischer esterification to give
why: Acid-catalysed esterification of ethanol with acetic acid produces ethyl acetate and water.
